questions.prompt: What is the single job of the Interface Adapters layer?

options.text: To hold the enterprise business rules
To convert data between the inner (use-case/entity) form and the outer (web/DB/UI) form

questions.explanation: Interface Adapters are a two-way translation membrane, converting data between the form use cases like and the form external agencies like.

questions.prompt: Match each adapter to what it converts.

pairs.right: External input → a use-case request model
A use-case response model → a view model

questions.explanation: Controllers take input in, presenters format output out, and gateways translate between entities and storage.

questions.prompt: SQL and ORM code belong in a ______ (the repository implementation), never in a use case or entity.
questions.explanation: Gateways in the Interface Adapters layer are the only place database code lives.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the Frameworks & Drivers layer are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It contains volatile details like the web framework, database, and UI
You should write as little code there as possible — mostly glue and config
It is where business rules should live
It is kept at arm's length so it stays replaceable

questions.explanation: The outer ring holds replaceable details with minimal code. Business rules must NOT live there.

questions.prompt: Order the components a request passes through, from the outside in and back out.
questions.explanation: Control enters at the controller, runs the use case (which uses a gateway), then the presenter formats a view model the humble view renders.

questions.prompt: Why keep controllers thin (no business rules)?

options.text: So business rules stay in use cases (reusable across delivery mechanisms) and the framework stays swappable
So the database can be the core of the system
Because presenters require it by law

questions.explanation: A fat controller traps rules in the web framework, killing reuse (e.g., by a CLI or job) and coupling logic to the framework.
